title: Every breath says your name
takeaway: When love is complete, there's no 'me' left, only you.
scene: The poet describes the place where the saqi, the one who pours love, has set up camp. Everyone gathers there, strict and free-spirited alike.

original: اوہ ساقی محبوب دلاں دا جس تھاں لائے ڈیرے
زاہد عارف رل کے پاون نال رنداں دے پھیرے
transliteration: Oh saaqi mehboob dilaan da jis thaan laaye dere
Zaahid aarif ral ke paavan naal rindaan de phere
translation: Wherever that saqi, beloved of hearts, sets up camp,
the strict and the wise walk round it together with the free spirits.
couplets.story: Wherever this saqi stops, people come. The strict religious types, the wise mystics and the carefree free spirits all end up there together, walking around the same place.

original: ساہ ساہ سجناں بولے تیرے لوں لوں تیرا ہوکا
میں کتھے ہن توں ای توں ایں او لھے نیں بس تیرے
transliteration: Saah saah sajnaan bole tere, loon loon tera hooka
Main kitthe, hun toon ee toon ain, o lekhe nain bas tere
translation: My love, every breath speaks of you; every pore cries out for you.
Where is 'I'? Now there's only you, only you; all my accounts are yours.
couplets.story: Every breath he takes says the Beloved's name. Every tiny part of his body calls out for them. Then he asks a deep question: where am 'I' now? There's nothing left of him, only the Beloved. Everything he is belongs to them.

original: علموں ادبوں شعر اچیرے آپے تر دے آون
میریاں سوچاں دے پنچھی جد آ کے بہن بنیرے
transliteration: Ilmon adabon shair uchere aape tur de aavan
Meriyaan sochaan de panchhi jad aa ke behan banere
translation: Lofty verses of learning and grace come walking in on their own,
when the birds of my thoughts come and perch on the rooftop.
couplets.story: He describes how his poems arrive. He doesn't force them. His thoughts are like birds that land on the roof, and then beautiful lines just come by themselves.

original: میریاں تیریاں سوچاں آخر اک مک کیوں ہو جاون
میں گلیاں دا واسو سجناں تیرے محل اچیرے
transliteration: Meriyaan teriyaan sochaan aakhir ik mik kyon ho jaavan
Main galiyaan da vaasu sajnaan, tere mehal uchere
translation: Why would your thoughts and mine ever become one?
My love, I live in the back lanes, and your palaces are high.
couplets.story: He wonders how they could ever think alike. He lives in the narrow streets, and the Beloved lives in a tall palace. They're worlds apart.

original: اپنے آل دوالے کولوں ایہو شکوہ مینوں
جنہاں روشن ہوندا جاواں ودھدے جان ہنیرے
transliteration: Apne aal dawaale kolon eho shikwa mainu
Jinna roshan honda jaavaan, vadhde jaan hanere
translation: This is my one complaint about the world around me:
the brighter I become, the more the darkness grows.
couplets.story: He has one complaint about the people around him. The more he tries to shine and do good, the darker things around him seem to get. Light makes the shadows easier to see.

original: ویکھ فوارہ خون تیرے دا کوئی اکھ نئیں پجھی
اس وستی دے لوکاں دے نیں مجھوں بھارے جیرے
transliteration: Vekh fawwaara khoon tere da koi akh nahin bhijji
Is vasti de lokaan de nain majhon bhaare jeere
translation: Seeing your blood gush out, not a single eye grew wet.
The people of this town have hearts heavier and duller than buffaloes.
couplets.story: He describes someone suffering terribly, bleeding, and nobody in town even cried. The people here have become so hard and dull that nothing moves them.

original: زندہ تے تابندہ رہندے روز حشر تک اوہو
جیہڑے صدق سلوک دے احمدؔ چکی پھرن پھریرے
transliteration: Zinda te taabinda rehnde roz-e-hashr tak oho
Jehre sidq sulook de Ahmad chukki phiran phareere
translation: Only they stay alive and shining until Judgment Day,
Ahmad, who carry the flag of sincerity and the spiritual path.
couplets.story: He ends with a promise. Some people will be remembered and keep shining until the end of time. They are the ones who stay sincere and keep walking the path toward God, holding it up like a flag.

deeper:
The second couplet is one of the deepest in the book. 'Where is I? Now there's only You' describes fana, the Sufi idea of the self dissolving in God until only God remains. 'Every breath speaks of You' is the practice of remembering God with every breath, which some Sufi orders teach directly.

The last couplet names the path outright: sidq (sincerity) and suluk (walking toward God). The 'saqi' who gathers both the strict worshipper and the free spirit is God, whose love draws in every kind of person.
why: In a few lines it goes from the very personal (every breath) to the social (a town that doesn't cry) to the eternal (until Judgment Day).
prompt: When do you feel most 'lost' in something good, so lost you forget yourself for a while?
notes: Couplet 6 describes 'your blood gushing'. It may refer to a specific killing or to the beloved's suffering; it is kept general.
